ImageDescription.value:
A cashmere sweater is a type of knitted garment made from the soft and fine wool of the cashmere goat. Cashmere wool is known for its exceptional softness, warmth, and durability, making it one of the most luxurious and sought-after materials in the fashion industry.

Cashmere sweaters come in a variety of styles, such as crew neck, v-neck, turtleneck, cardigan, and more. They are available in a wide range of colors, from neutral shades like black, gray, and beige to bold and bright colors like red, pink, and blue.

Cashmere sweaters are prized for their lightweight and breathable nature, making them comfortable to wear all year round. They are also hypoallergenic, making them a great option for those with sensitive skin.

To care for a cashmere sweater, it is recommended to hand wash it in cold water using a mild detergent, and then lay it flat to dry. Avoid wringing or twisting the sweater as this can damage the delicate fibers. With proper care, a cashmere sweater can last for many years and remain a luxurious and timeless addition to any wardrobe.

The Sierra Madre News is the longest, continuous running newspaper in the City of Sierra Madre. It was published from October 1906 to June 1999. The newspaper was published by R. T. Cowles and yearly subscriptions cost $1.50. Successive editors include: C.W. Hill, George Morgridge, L.R. Goshorn. Clifford C. Ward, Peter Ward, Edgar W. Jenkinson, William F. Thomas, Ed E. Herwig, R. Robert Evans, Jannene G. Reed, and Michael De Wees. The paper was printed with a hand press, and then a two-revolution cylinder press, and starting in 1947 a 52-inch Miehle flat bed double revolution press, and finally using the offset method.
For additional information see <a href="https://californiarevealed.org/islandora/object/cavpp%3A147823" rel="nofollow">California Revealed</a>.
